# A ball that contains an interval, one-limb bounds

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone2/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `interval_to_ball_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A ball of center $c$ and radius $r$ that contains the interval $[x_l, x_u]$: the whole line for an unbounded interval, the empty set for the empty one:

$$[c - r, c + r] \supseteq [x_l, x_u].$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Ball<T, 1>(X)` | `Interval<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>` | explicit; `constexpr`; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED (a constructor does not take it).

## Requires

- $[x_l, x_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $x_l = +\infty$ and $x_u = -\infty$, or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $x_l \le x_u$, $x_l < +\infty$, $x_u > -\infty$, each bound a number of `T` or an infinity; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The ball of center $c$ and radius $r$ is canonical, and empty exactly when the interval is.
- If $[x_l, x_u]$ is bounded: $c$ and $r$ are finite, $x_l \le c \le x_u$, $\lvert c - \tfrac{x_l + x_u}{2}\rvert \le u\,\lvert \tfrac{x_l + x_u}{2}\rvert + \eta$, and $[c - r, c + r] \supseteq [x_l, x_u]$: $r$ is the smallest number of `T` with that property, $\mathrm{RU}(\max(c - x_l, x_u - c))$. It is then a finite ball.
- An unbounded interval gives the whole line, center 0 and radius $+\infty$ (a ball cannot be a half-line); the empty set gives the empty ball, every limb a NaN.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `interval_to_ball_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalConvert.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalConvert.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions interval_to_ball_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `interval_to_ball_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** interval_mid_rad_1, an unbounded interval made the whole line (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/interval_to_ball_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/interval_to_ball_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`interval_mid_rad_1`](interval_mid_rad_1.md).

```
# A ball with a one-limb center that contains an interval with one-limb bounds (milestone2.md, "One
# enclosure interface", "Midpoint, radius and the conversions", "Interval to ball"):
# interval_mid_rad_1, then one select. A bounded interval gives the ball of its midpoint and radius,
# the smallest radius of T for that center; an unbounded one, whose radius is +inf, the whole line,
# whose center is 0 and not the +-Omega of a half-line; the empty set gives two NaN already, the
# empty ball. So the ball is canonical, contains the interval, and is empty exactly when the
# interval is. (The page speaks of two selects; the second, of the empty set, is the one that
# interval_mid_rad_1 has already made.)

(m, r) = interval_mid_rad_1(xl, xu)
un     = eq(r, const inf)
c      = select(un, 0, m)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#interval_to_ball_1)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 4 domains of 4 formats | 581 154 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
